title: Device configuration file can hold another device's settings and restoring it changes that device
description:
Observed in INDIGO A1 (embedded server, trace log of 2026-11-16 20:59:05): with Imager Agent ADDITIONAL_INSTANCES set to 2 and CCD Imager Simulator selected in Imager Agent, selecting CCD Guider Simulator in Imager Agent #2 sets ADDITIONAL_INSTANCES of Imager Agent to 0 and the additional instances disappear.

Trace: Imager Agent #2 sends CONFIG.LOAD to CCD Guider Simulator; the file .indigo/CCD_Guider_Simulator.config is opened and contains no simulator settings but properties with device='Imager Agent' (AGENT_IMAGER_BATCH, AGENT_IMAGER_FOCUS, AGENT_IMAGER_FOCUS_FAILURE, AGENT_IMAGER_FOCUS_ESTIMATOR, ADDITIONAL_INSTANCES COUNT=0, AGENT_PROCESS_FEATURES, AGENT_IMAGER_SELECTION), exactly the content and order written by save_config() of indigo_agent_imager.c. CONFIG_READER then enumerates and changes 'Imager Agent'.ADDITIONAL_INSTANCES. Not reproducible on a server whose simulator config file is intact.

Two defects in indigo_libs/indigo_driver.c:
1. Configuration restore does not check the device. config_restore_collect() queues every property found in the file and config_restore_handler() dispatches it with the device name from the file, so a config file of device A can change device B. Seen directly in the code and in the trace.
2. A device's settings were written into another device's config file. How is not visible in the trace (it happened earlier). Hypothesis, not verified: indigo_open_config_file() and test_config_file() build the path in a function-level 'static char path[512]', so two threads working with configuration at the same time (an agent saving its config while a selected device connects and tests or opens its own) can open the path computed by the other thread.

Expected: restoring the configuration of a device changes only that device (entries for other devices are ignored, and reported in the log), and a property is always saved to the config file of its own device, also under concurrent saves and loads.

Reproduce first: a test that restores a config file containing an entry for another device and shows that device changed; for defect 2, verify or refute the static-buffer hypothesis (for example concurrent save and open for two devices) before changing the code.

outcome.summary:
Reviewed diff master...HEAD (371663c71, clean worktree): indigo_libs/indigo_driver.c, indigo_test/unit/test_profile_selection.c, indigo_docs/DRIVER_DEVELOPMENT_BASICS.md.

DEFECT (acceptance 'restoring the configuration of a device changes only that device' not met): the device filter is applied only in config_restore_collect() (indigo_driver.c:604), i.e. the CONFIG.LOAD path. The other restore path, indigo_load_properties() -> load_properties(device, ..., NULL, NULL) (indigo_driver.c:527-528), still passes dispatch=NULL, so indigo_xml_parse_with_callback() uses indigo_change_property (indigo_xml.c:1433) and every entry in the file is routed to whatever device it names. This path restores configuration on attach for agent_imager (indigo_agent_imager.c:2903), agent_guider (:2793), agent_mount (:2227), agent_astrometry (:1188), agent_platesolver (:564), agent_alpaca (:1226) and the server device (indigo_server.c:1209). Agent attach also runs for additional instances (e.g. 'Imager Agent #2'), so a corrupted Imager_Agent_#2.config holding 'Imager Agent'.ADDITIONAL_INSTANCES COUNT=0 (the same corruption defect 2 produced) would still set the base agent's ADDITIONAL_INSTANCES to 0 on instance attach - the reported symptom. Correction: apply the same device-name check (skip + log) inside load_properties() for both dispatch modes, e.g. a filtering dispatch wrapper used when reader == NULL, and extend the restore test to cover indigo_load_properties(). The docs sentence (DRIVER_DEVELOPMENT_BASICS.md:572) is accurate for CONFIG.LOAD only; once both paths filter it can say so, otherwise it should not imply the synchronous helper is covered.

Verified OK: static path[512] -> local in test_config_file, indigo_open_config_file, indigo_remove_properties removes the shared-buffer race; no other function-level static path buffers remain in the config save/load path (make_config_file_name writes into caller buffers; indigo_xml_escape_b buffers are INDIGO_THREAD_LOCAL). restore->devic

Round 2, reviewed diff master...HEAD at ccb697be1 (tree 9d5407672, no uncommitted changes); whitespace and unit checks recorded as passed on this tree (flow status).

Round 1 finding resolved: load_properties() with reader == NULL now allocates config_load_context (indigo_adapter_context first, so the cast and the parser's use of client_context as indigo_adapter_context are valid), copies device->name, and parses with config_load_dispatch, which logs and skips entries whose device differs and otherwise calls indigo_change_property exactly like the previous default (indigo_xml.c:1433). Allocation/free: both .common and .config blocks malloc sizeof(config_load_context) and free the same pointer after parsing; no early return between them, the parser returns void, and the close/free sequence is unchanged, so no leak on parse failure. CONFIG.LOAD path unaffected: reader != NULL keeps reader->client_context and the passed dispatch (config_restore_collect), which keeps its own device filter. The only callers are indigo_load_properties (NULL, NULL) and start_config_restore (reader, collect), so ignoring 'dispatch' when reader == NULL changes no caller.

Test: 'restore ignores entries of other devices' now resets both devices' PROFILE_NAME, calls indigo_load_properties(&owner, false) on the same file (foreign entry first, own second), waits for the owner's 'Own profile' and then asserts the other device still has 'Untouched profile' after a further 200 ms; this exercises the synchronous path, and the ticket note records it failing with the filter removed. Docs sentence (DRIVER_DEVELOPMENT_BASICS.md:572) now accurately covers CONFIG and indigo_load_properties(). Formatting follows AGENTS.md (tabs, braces, single-line calls, no blank lines in function bodies).

Non-blocking nits: the test assigns 'device = &other;' twice in a row and performs an unexplained indigo_enumerate_properties(&client, &filter) for the other device; neither affects the result. Not covered: I did not r

Round 3 (reworked scope), reviewed HEAD 0cf5324d0, tree b2f84ddad, clean worktree. Supersedes my earlier pass, which was recorded on this tree without review.

Scope: diff master...HEAD is 2 files. indigo_libs/indigo_driver.c changes only the three function-level 'static char path[512]' -> locals in test_config_file (:451), indigo_open_config_file (:459) and indigo_remove_properties (:928); the read-side filter (config_restore device_name, config_restore_collect check, config_load_context/dispatch) is gone and those parts are identical to master. indigo_docs/DRIVER_DEVELOPMENT_BASICS.md is identical to master. test_profile_selection.c adds only 'config paths are not shared between threads'.

Correctness: the shared static path buffer was the cross-thread state that let one thread open (O_TRUNC on create) a path computed for another device; with locals, make_config_file_name writes only to the caller's buffer. Independent write-path audit found no other shared mutable state: indigo_uni_create_file/open_file/mkdir/is_readable/remove use only locals (indigo_uni_io.c:492-530, 2585-2655), handle index via next_handle_index, indigo_xml_escape_b buffers are INDIGO_THREAD_LOCAL, property_save_file_handle and config_mutex are per device. The only remaining shared statics on the path are the lazily filled indigo_uni_config_folder()/home_folder() buffers (same content for every caller; partial-read only on a racing first call) - observation, not this defect.

Test: deterministic after the fix (any mismatch is a real cross-thread path mix-up, 0 expected), isolated (private home, own synthetic names, file removed), and per the ticket notes fails on master with ~399000/600000 mismatches - adequate reproduction-first evidence of the root cause. Dropping the end-to-end indigo_save_property race test is acceptable: an ineffective (never failing) test would add no evidence. Formatting matches AGENTS.md. whitespace and unit checks passed on tree b2f84ddad (flow status).

Reading config save/load path in indigo_driver.c
Implementation resumed: the review requested changes

Review round 1: indigo_load_properties() (reader==NULL) now uses config_load_dispatch, which skips and logs entries of other devices. Test 'restore ignores entries of other devices' extended: after resetting both devices' PROFILE_NAME, indigo_load_properties(owner) with a foreign entry. Before (filter removed): FAIL at the new assertion (foreign device changed); after: PASS in 3 runs. Docs sentence broadened to cover both paths.

Owner scope change (2026-11-16): do not solve how to prevent reading a damaged config file; solve how not to produce it. The read-side device filter (CONFIG.LOAD and indigo_load_properties paths), its tests and its documentation sentence are out of scope and are to be removed from the change. In scope: a property is always written to its own device's config file, also under concurrent saves and loads (defect 2), with reproduction-first evidence.
Reverting read-side filter, auditing write path

Scope rework: read-side filter removed (indigo_load_properties/config_restore/docs/restore test identical to master). Write-side audit: static path[512] in test_config_file/indigo_open_config_file/indigo_remove_properties is the only shared mutable state found on the write path (verified: escape buffers are thread-local, handle index is mutex-protected, property_save_file_handle and config_mutex are per device, make_config_file_name writes only to the caller buffer). Deterministic test 'config paths are not shared between threads' fails on master (~399000 mismatches) and passes after. An end-to-end test of two threads saving via indigo_save_property into their own files (5000 and 60000 iterations each) did NOT fail on master's static buffer: the window between building the path and open() is too small to hit with file I/O, so that test was dropped as ineffective. Unverified suspicion: indigo_save_property() picks the file from property->device and caches the handle per device, so a caller passing a foreign-device property writes into that device's file (by design, no concurrency needed).

An end-to-end test of two threads saving via indigo_save_property into their own files (5000 and 60000 iterations each) did NOT fail on master's static buffer: the window between building the path and open() is too small to hit with file I/O, so that test was dropped as ineffective. Unverified suspicion: indigo_save_property() picks the file from property->device and caches the handle per device, so a caller passing a foreign-device property writes into that device's file (by design, no concurrency needed).
